structures.name: Frontal Lobe
structures.about: The most rostral lobe of the cerebrum. Seen from the side it forms the front third of the hemisphere, ending at the frontal pole.

structures.name: Parietal Lobe
structures.about: The lobe on the dorsal convexity behind the frontal lobe. It integrates somatosensory information and contributes to spatial awareness.

structures.name: Occipital Lobe
structures.about: The caudal lobe of the cerebrum, overlying the cerebellum. It contains the primary visual cortex.

structures.name: Occipital Pole
structures.about: The caudal tip of the cerebral hemisphere, where the occipital lobe ends just rostral to the cerebellum.

structures.name: Cerebellum
structures.about: The folded mass caudal and ventral to the occipital lobe. It coordinates posture, balance, and the timing of movement.

structures.name: Insula
structures.about: Cortex buried in the depth of the lateral sulcus, overlapped by the surrounding lobes. It contributes to visceral sensation and autonomic control.

structures.name: Temporal Lobe
structures.about: The ventrolateral lobe of the cerebrum, below the lateral sulcus. It carries auditory cortex and, deeper, the hippocampus.

structures.name: Rhinencephalon
structures.about: The olfactory brain: the ventrolateral cortex ventral to the rhinal fissure, prominent in sheep and other macrosmatic animals.

structures.name: Rhinal Fissure
structures.about: The groove along the ventrolateral surface separating the rhinencephalon below from the neocortex above.

structures.name: Pons
structures.about: The bulge on the ventral brainstem between the midbrain and the medulla. Its transverse fibers carry cortical information to the cerebellum.

structures.name: Medulla
structures.about: The most caudal part of the brainstem, continuous with the spinal cord. It houses centers for breathing, heart rate, and other vital reflexes.
